 Dillon Brooks had 22 points (9-of-12 FGs), a rebound, two assists, a steal, and four 3-pointers in 20 minutes before getting ejected on Friday. 
 Dillon Brooks was hitting his shots and was a big reason they stayed in this game. He kicked out his leg on a jump shot which was viewed as excessive and resulted in a flagrant 2 foul and an ejection. Obviously the ejection isn’t great but it is part of the deal with Brooks. Even with it, he still put up a lot of points and could’ve had an even better line. His next opportunity to play will be on Monday against the Warriors. 
 Dillon Brooks 
 PHX 
 Guard-Forward 
 #3 
 Dillon Brooks finished Monday’s loss to the Thunder with 19 points (4-of-14 FGs, 8-of-12 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers. 
 Brooks didn’t have a good night shooting the basketball, making three of his ten three-point attempts and going 4-of-14 overall. The good news is that he recorded a complete stat line, which is welcome for a player whose fantasy value has underwhelmed so far. Brooks’ 2025-26 output factored into his preseason ADP, as he exceeded many fantasy managers’ expectations last season. 
 Dillon Brooks 
 PHX 
 Guard-Forward 
 #3 
 Dillon Brooks recorded 10 points (4-of-11 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Brooks was one of three Suns starters in double figures, but Wednesday’s 124-83 defeat was one to forget. “The Villain” recorded no assists or defensive stats and struggled with his shooting. Brooks, who will likely offer late-round value at best in category leagues this season, will look to redeem himself on Saturday when Phoenix hosts Golden State. 
 Dillon Brooks 
 PHX 
 Guard-Forward 
 #3 
 Dillon Brooks tallied 24 points (7-of-9 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bulls. 
 While the Suns’ other primary scoring options struggled on Wednesday, Brooks did not. “The Villain,” who was a pleasant surprise in fantasy basketball last season, shot 3-of-5 from beyond the arc and made all four of his two-point attempts. Unfortunately, Brooks was also responsible for five turnovers, but the offensive output is what stood out the most. He remains a late-round option in standard leagues, and Brooks’ floor may be appealing to risk-averse managers. 
 Dillon Brooks 
 PHX 
 Guard-Forward 
 #3 
 Dillon Brooks agreed to a three-year, $73 million contract extension, reports ESPN’s Shams Charania. 
 Brooks only played 56 games last year, breaking a streak of three consecutive seasons with at least 72 games played. Still, Brooks averaged a career-high 20.2 points per game in his first year in Phoenix. That seems to have made an impression as the Suns decided to lock up the 30-year-old guard for the foreseeable future. With the team bringing in Miles Bridges and Luke Kennard this offseason, it could be tough to repeat the usage that led to his career-high scoring. 
 Dillon Brooks 
 PHX 
 Guard-Forward 
 #3 
 Dillon Brooks amassed 33 points (11-of-21 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers in Saturday’s Game 3 loss to the Thunder. 
 After an inefficient Game 1 performance, Brooks has produced consecutive 30-point games. In Game 3, the veteran wing shot a little over 50 percent from the field and led the Suns in field-goal attempts. With Devin Booker struggling and being the focal point of Oklahoma City’s defensive approach, there have been more opportunities for Brooks. While some may want him to tone down the aggressiveness as far as the shot selection is concerned, he’s been effective in back-to-back games. 
 Dillon Brooks 
 PHX 
 Guard-Forward 
 #3 
 Dillon Brooks tallied 30 points (12-of-23 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 Brooks bounced back from a very inefficient 18-point performance in Game 1 by hitting the 30-point mark on above 50.0 percent shooting, leading to half of his scoring total. He didn’t make any big splashes in other statistical categories, but his three-point contributions and scoring were big positives nonetheless. The series will flip to Phoenix on Saturday, when Brooks and the Suns will look to avoid going down three games. 
 Dillon Brooks 
 PHX 
 Guard-Forward 
 #3 
 Dillon Brooks tallied 18 points (6-of-22 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 1 loss to the Thunder. 
 Given what he brings to the table defensively, Brooks earns a certain level of freedom on the offensive end of the floor. However, there’s no reason why he should lead the Suns in shot attempts when Devin Booker and Jalen Green are available. In Game 1, Brooks put up 22 shots, with Booker next in line with 17 attempts and Green finishing with 16. That’s something to keep an eye on moving forward, beginning with Wednesday’s Game 2. If the Thunder defense can funnel things towards Brooks consistently, this series could be a sweep. 
 Dillon Brooks 
 PHX 
 Guard-Forward 
 #3 
 Dillon Brooks logged 20 points (6-of-10 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Brooks had a positive impact in his 37 minutes on Tuesday before fouling out late in the fourth quarter. While on the floor, he was a pest defensively, as shown in his four steals, but also repeatedly made momentum-building shots while the Suns led. Despite taking only 10 shots on the evening, the veteran forward finished as one of three Suns players to tally at least 20 points. Phoenix will hope Brooks can be productive again on Friday against the winner of Wednesday’s Warriors-Clippers matchup. 
 Devin Booker 
 PHX 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Devin Booker (ankle), Dillon Brooks (hand), Grayson Allen (hamstring) and Royce O’Neale (knee) are out for Sunday’s game against the Thunder. 
 While Booker, Brooks and O’Neale are sitting for injury-management reasons, Allen is out with a left hamstring injury he sustained during Friday’s loss to the Lakers. As for Saturday evening, the Suns were still listing the issue as a sore hamstring, but that’s something to keep an eye on ahead of Tuesday’s play-in game. Rasheer Fleming, Amir Coffey and Koby Brea are three wings who are in line to play rotation minutes on Sunday.

 Charles Bassey recorded 19 points (7-of-10 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), eight rebounds and one assist in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 While Bassey scored nine points in the first half, his role in the Warriors’ rotation grew more important in the second half. Draymond Green was ejected two minutes into the third quarter, giving Bassey more minutes. In 15 second-half minutes, he accumulated 10 points, six rebounds and one assist. Bassey’s 19 points are a career high, and more nights like this would go a long way toward making his contract fully guaranteed come January 10.

 Brandin Podziemski recorded 20 points (7-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 Podziemski recorded his second 20-point game of the season on Monday, finishing one point shy of his high (21 vs. the Lakers on Friday). Like Stephen Curry, Podz was most effective during the third quarter, scoring 10 points on 4-of-6 shooting from the field. The negative for fantasy managers is that Podziemski didn’t provide much value beyond the points and three-pointers. They’ll hope for more on Thursday when the Warriors host the Heat.

 Stephen Curry tallied 34 points (9-of-21 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 While he didn’t have his best night shooting the basketball, Curry extended his streak of games with at least 31 points to three. The Warriors star was at his best in the third quarter, shooting 6-of-9 from the field and scoring 18 points. Outside that period, the Suns kept Curry in check, but he still went home with a stat line that many fantasy managers will take without hesitation.

 Austin Reaves lit up the Heat with 27 points (10-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, five assists, four three-pointers and five turnovers on Monday.
 The last few games had been rough for Reaves, but he was able to get back on track in this one. The turnovers still weren’t great, and he now has 24 over his last four outings. However, he was far more efficient as a scorer, which helped the Lakers secure a second win in as many days. Reaves has been a high-level second option behind Luka Dončić this season, though the turnovers need to be cleaned up for him to match his production from last year.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 42 points (14-of-24 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), seven rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and six three-pointers in a 138-117 win over the Heat on Monday.
 It has been an unreal start to the season for Dončić, and Monday’s performance was just another chapter. He has scored at least 35 points and knocked down at least six three-pointers in each of his last five appearances, while going for at least 40 in four of those outings. The one game he didn’t score 40, he had 37, which was also the only game during this stretch where he shot below 50 percent from the floor. Dončić set a new season high for assists in this game as well. He has been an elite offensive engine, and he’ll look to stay hot against the Kings on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Walker Kessler recorded a double-double on Monday with 15 points (7-of-13 FGs), 15 rebounds, two assists and two steals against the Heat.
 Kessler has finally started dominating the glass. He has recorded three straight double-doubles and has at least 15 points and 15 rebounds in each of his last two outings. Kessler has been exactly what the Lakers have needed, and it has worked out well for fantasy managers as well. With Luka Dončić running the offense, Kessler should continue to be a fantasy star.

 Davion Mitchell finished with 15 points (5-of-5 FGs), seven assists, one block and four three-pointers on Monday against the Lakers.
 While Mitchell had a spectacular game, volume was an issue. He didn’t miss a shot from the floor, but he only took five shots. Mitchell has had an excellent start to the year, but his lack of shot attempts prevented him from having a better night. However, he continues to dish out the dimes at a high rate, which has been the driving factor behind his top-75 value to start this season.
